_comment: Release policy: the half of the update manifest a human decides.
`python run.py publish` merges this with the facts it measures from the
built artefacts -- version, sha256, size -- and writes
deploy/uat/downloads/manifest.json. Facts are never typed here, because a
hand-copied checksum is how you ship an update every client refuses.
READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING EITHER FLAG. The backend now serves the answer on
every API response and every connector frame, so what you write here
reaches the whole fleet within one request rather than within six hours.
There is no longer a poll interval standing between a mistake and everyone.
min_supported_version is the kill switch. A client older than this is
refused with 426 and told to update, rather than failing in whatever way
the wire change happens to break it. Raise it only when an old client
genuinely cannot be served -- it locks people out of their own accounting
data until they act. If you raise it wrongly, the recovery is
TALLYFLOW_ENFORCE_MIN_APP_VERSION=false, which restores service without
waiting for a corrected manifest to reach every phone.
mandatory means the update installs without asking (connector) or blocks
the app until taken (mobile). Reserve it for security fixes and wire
breaks; a shop that gets an unrequested restart mid-day remembers it.
Note for the connector: mandatory -- or being below the floor -- installs
even where the operator set auto_update:false. That setting means 'do not
interrupt my shop for routine releases', not 'leave me on a build that
reports the wrong figures'.

connector.notes: Moves this computer to the new TallyFlow server address. Nothing about how it reads Tally has changed. Marked mandatory because the old address is being retired: a connector that skipped this build would keep dialling a name that stops answering, and could not then be reached to be told anything.

android.notes: A tighter layout throughout -- more rows on screen without scrolling. Fixes a dashboard that came up blank when the period had something to compare against. Points at the new server address.
